I also advise my sisters to do this as well, but I don't know if they (or their husbands) swapped them out, if they even have room.

Where did you get your used rim and how did you make sure it fit? Is only the diameter and number of nuts important?

I found the same car that was couple years older in a scrapyard. The rim I found was the same factory room I already had, part number and all.

As for size, there's a couple numbers you want to look at. Obviously the bolt pattern and diameter need to match. There's also width and offset.

Ideally, the width and offset should match your current rims to have an identical spare. However, you do have a bit of play here and it's not there end of the world if it's not there exact same. It is a spare rim after all.

So a tire can fit on several widths. If you have 8 inch wide rims, you'll be fine with an 8.5 inch spare. I don't think this 1/2 inch wide affect tire diameter, but if it does, it won't be nearly as much as putting a new tires on the same axle as a used tire.

Now there's also rim offset or backspacing. These are two different ways to measure the same thing, how far the rim sticks out. See how far this rim sticks out. That's because this guy has ridiculous backspacing.
